$comment: Rails for EVERY claude ORCHESTRATOR session — the `claude -p` in
`ralph.sh` that reads tickets and comments. `ralph.sh` adds it with
`--settings` whenever the orchestrator runner is claude; a role that
names its own `orchestratorSettings` in `roles.ts` carries that file
INSTEAD, so every role file must contain every rule here
(`claude-executor-rails.test.ts` checks the superset).
The iteration runs under the project's secrets manager with the withheld
names (`secrets.withhold` in `.ralph/config.json`) stripped from its
environment. The manager's CLI is still authenticated on the host, so a
session that ran it by hand would get every withheld value back. The
executor has been denied that since its rails existed
(`claude-executor-settings.json`); this file is the same rule for the
session that reads untrusted ticket text.
Both spellings, `Bash(x *)` and `Bash(x:*)`, for the reason
`claude-executor-settings.json` gives. Like that file's path rules it is a
tripwire, not a boundary: `env doppler …` or a token read out of
`~/.doppler` would go round it. The boundary is a manager config that does
not hold the withheld names at all.
The tracker credential directory (`tracker/credentials.ts`) is denied for
the same reason: a Linear or Jira token lives there, and the session
reaches the tracker only through `tracker.ts`, which reads it itself.
The Slack plugin's settings directory (`plugins/slack/plugin.ts`) holds a
bot token, and is denied the same way. So is the screenshot credential
directory (`ui-shots.ts`): it holds a test account's password, and the
session reaches it only through `ui-shots.ts capture`, which reads it itself.
